system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: The periodic HTTPS activity is attributable to a ChartMate-named updater running as ben.carter from C:\Users\ben.carter\AppData\Local\ChartMate\cmupdate.exe, rather than from the approved inventory path under C:\Program Files.

The updater contacted update.chartmate-imaging.net, whereas the inventory identifies update.chartmate-imaging.com as the approved update endpoint. The observed .net endpoint is not established as approved by the supplied context.

The .net endpoint was contacted repeatedly at roughly five-minute intervals from 13:38 through 14:08 UTC; proxy records show successful tunnels as well as a 407 authentication-required response and a 502 gateway error.

Sysmon network events associate the repeated proxy connections with PID 3416, the AppData ChartMate-named executable, supporting that the updater process—not merely unrelated browser traffic—made the connections.
A separate SMB connection from WS-BCARTER-01 to FILE-HD-01 was followed by a FILE-HD-01 network logon recorded as ANONYMOUS LOGON; its purpose is not apparent in these records.

The updater process generated a file-create event targeting its own executable path shortly after a successful connection. This merits investigation but does not, by itself, establish what file content was written.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records show CONNECT destinations, status, byte counts, and duration, but the supplied records do not show HTTPS contents or the data exchanged inside successful tunnels (for example, T015-00110 and T015-00209).

The supplied records do not include a hash, signature, or content analysis for the AppData executable; the process path and file-create event alone do not establish its integrity (T015-00108, T015-00114).
The SMB records establish a connection and an ANONYMOUS LOGON event, but do not identify the share, requested files, or operation performed (T015-00253, T015-00257).
claims_not_established: Whether the AppData executable is authentic ChartMate software or a malicious lookalike.
Whether update.chartmate-imaging.net is controlled by ChartMate or otherwise authorized by the organization.
What content, if any, was transferred through the successful HTTPS tunnels.
What SMB resource or operation caused the anonymous logon to FILE-HD-01.
Whether the activity resulted in execution of a malicious payload, data access, or data exfiltration.
additional_evidence_needed: Acquire and preserve the AppData executable; calculate its hash and verify its digital signature and provenance against a trusted ChartMate source.
Confirm with the application owner or vendor whether update.chartmate-imaging.net and this per-user installation path are authorized.
Collect proxy/TLS inspection, endpoint network, and file telemetry sufficient to determine the updater's requests, responses, and any files it downloaded or changed.
Review FILE-HD-01 SMB/share and authentication auditing around 13:54 UTC to identify the resource and operation associated with the anonymous logon.
Correlate endpoint security detections and process/file activity on WS-BCARTER-01 before and after the observed updater execution.
